compatibility_questions_requiring_differ.finding: The upstream key fingerprint canonicalizes integers, but retains raw scalar spelling for bool/null/float keys. The new Vec visitor has no second semantic equality check. It may accept true/True, null/~, or 1.0/1.00 in one map where the former serde_yaml::Value map rejects repeated resolved keys. Existing six utility tests cover exact same-string duplicates, not these aliases.

compatibility_questions_requiring_differ.finding: strict_booleans uses eq_ignore_ascii_case; TrUe parses as bool. Do not claim full YAML1.2 spelling equivalence without comparing the old parser and defining this behavior.
compatibility_questions_requiring_differ.status: New behavior verified from implementation, old differential pending.

confirmed_from_primary_source: Tagged captures parser-resolved tags and delegates kind parsing with the existing configuration; root/key tag transparency and application value-tag suppression match the explicit consumer design.
Strict booleans preserves yes/OFF as strings; true/false are recognized case-insensitively.
Integer/f64 dispatch matches the implemented visitor variants; nonfinite floats pass to the explicit canonical rendering.
Duplicate key processing occurs in MapAccess before the Vec visitor, so exact duplicated string keys and integer spelling aliases are not silently admitted.
The visitor consumes every nested sequence and mapping even when keys/values are discarded; invalid UTF8 is rejected by from_slice.
AsOrdinary prevents merge expansion. Default budgets and alias limits remain enabled; optional include/property resolvers remain unset.
review_conclusion: Prepared parser follows the intended bounded scalar extraction, tags and merge design; do not mark full compatibility/promotion passed until differential boundaries and real consumers are verified. No production activation inferred.
